posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
When I'm introducing SOTM to new people, I find that the hardest thing to do is to explain the heroes that they have to choose from in a way that will instantly make sense.  I tend to fumble through awkward introductions, of which one notable example was me finding myself able to identify Bunker only as "the guy who needs a gun" in slightly more words than this, and having someone choose to play him on that basis.  When RC/IR shipped, I was pleased to note that the four heroes in the set did not get only biographical info, but also a little "How to play" section.

I think it would be a good idea to make up little cards or sheets of paper with very brief introduction info for all of the characters, to facilitate these kinds of choices.  These would be a nice accessory that you could include in your set if you were big on enrolling new players, rather than just having a steady playgroup.  So I'm opening this thread as a brainstorming and copywriting arena for the project.  The goal will be brevity, clarity, and immediate grokkability - this will be a way to get people into the game who know nothing about it, who aren't necessarily big on comic books or even familiar with card games (generally they will be gamers of some sort, but very little should be taken for granted).

posts.name: danmarshall14
posts.cooked:
The Hero Charts that Pydro linked are really great.  I think they have the potential to be a great tool to introducing new players.

But some of the info on the stat charts just seems incredibly off to me.  Like Unity has more in "Healing" than Legacy, The Scholar, and Haka while Ra has more in "Healing" than Tempest, even though Ra's healing is pretty situational (when his Staff is played) and only heals himself where Tempest has the more "practical" heal (heals your team and is a usable power).  Unity also has the same amount in "Deck Manipulation" as The Visionary, which is incredibly misleading.

I'm not sure how BGG got these stats (I'm assuming by counting the number of cards in the Hero deck that had any of those effects and adding them up), but I feel they don't truly represent how each hero really feels when you play them.  Again, its a great start and I'm glad someone took the time to put all that info together, but I feel there could be plenty of improvements (especially more newcomer friendly improvements who may be misled picking the wrong hero based on those stat charts)

If I was a newcomer being introduced to Sentinels, I would see "Deck Manipulation" as the ability to control all of the decks/cards on the field (scrying, drawing, discarding, shifting cards from the trash to the deck/visa versa) and I think we all know that if you want that sort of trait, you play as Visionary, not Unity.  I think balancing each heroes stats without tightening the definition of what each stat actually means (Healing, Support, Deck Manipulation, Buffing/Debuffing) can lead to newcomers thinking a hero is going to play a certain way only to find out otherwise.

Again, I am very glad someone took the time to create those stat charts and I'm sure it has come in handy several times.  I just thought I'd point out where I think the flaws lie and why.

Gives you a card draw, thins your deck, speeds up the chance of getting what you need for a given situation, ect ect.

BlueHairedMeerkat:

More generally, manipulating your own deck is basically just a way to accelerate your doing the other stuff your deck does.

Yup. Manipulating your own deck is a measure of how quickly you can set-up and/or how quick you can adapt to a new situation. Manipulating other decks (like the villain deck) is a way to slow down villain set-ups to buy you more time to adjust and react.

Where is the issue?

 

danmarshall14:

I think balancing each heroes stats without tightening the definition of what each stat actually means (Healing, Support, Deck Manipulation, Buffing/Debuffing) can lead to newcomers thinking a hero is going to play a certain way only to find out otherwise.

Tightening definitions on these things is really a fools errand. It is much better for everyones expectations to think of those terms generally, specifically because of how different all the decks are. Take healing for example. Unity has some great healing abilities, but they are for her and her bots, unlike Argent Adept or Tempest who can extend those heals to others AoE style. To tighten the definitions, you will ultimatley have to create a multitude of sub-catagories to accuratly describe the pragmatic functionality of these abilities. If the goal here is to be easy on newcommers, this really isn't the solution you want to entertain.

The issue is in using the same phrase to mean two different, non-interchangeable things. Yes, both things give you more ability to adjust. Extra card plays, damage reduction and healing let you mitigate damage and card destruction, giving you more time to adjust. Damage and ongoing destruction let you destroy villain threats, giving you more time to adjust.

And also, Ra has only a little manipulation of his own deck, and he requires no set-up; every card play is just a bonus to him. Unity, on the other hand, apparently has lots od deck manipulation, and yet is hard to set up and is one of the most likely heroes to draw two cards on her first turn. Deck manipulation =/= a speedy setup.

danmarshall14 wrote:
 

I think balancing each heroes stats without tightening the definition of what each stat actually means (Healing, Support, Deck Manipulation, Buffing/Debuffing) can lead to newcomers thinking a hero is going to play a certain way only to find out otherwise.

Unity has some great healing abilities, but they are for her and her bots, unlike Argent Adept or Tempest who can extend those heals to others AoE style. To tighten the definitions, you will ultimatley have to create a multitude of sub-catagories to accuratly describe the pragmatic functionality of these abilities. If the goal here is to be easy on newcommers, this really isn't the solution you want to entertain. 

I agree; the answer is not in separate categories for the same type of stat (like you said, Self Healing vs Team Healing) as that would get incredibly convulated, very quickly.  I'm not sure what the solution looks like yet, but for now I'm simply pointing out the flaws (that I see personally) in the current stat chart, mostly from the eyes of a newcomer.  I think when Absolute Zero and Legacy have the same stat for Healing, it can lead people to expect a different performance from the hero they pick.

Again going back to Ra who can heal 3 HP, but is conditional upon a Staff of Ra entering play, where Legacy or AA can heal multiple targets consistently as the ability stems from a power usable each turn.  Haka and Scholar can nuke heal with the right hand.  All the meanwhile, AA has the capability to heal a ridiculous amount to 3 targets on his turn through Silver Shadow combos, where Unity's is a small heal for her and her robots only.  And yet all these characters have nearly the exact same Heal stat.  Don't you see that as a little…flawed?  If you're going to put all healing under just one stat, that's perfectly fine, but having each of those characters representing the same amount of "Healing" is a problem in my eyes.  The healing capabilities of Unity is nowhere close to the self healing of Scholar/Haka or the team healing of AA.

And again, I do not know the method they used to obtain these stats.  I'm guessing they went through the deck and tallied up the effects each card grants and put the results on a chart.  But this obviously doesn't account for different card combinations or Powers staying on the field and healing consistently over the course of the game vs a one-time effect like Ra's Staff.

I just think the current stat placements paint the wrong picture for a lot of the heroes and am hoping we, as a community, can maybe pull our heads together to come up with something better.  Surely you think there's room for improvement?

From what I remember reading when I first downloaded the charts to add to my own cards, the creator counted the cards that had each effect. Simple as that, they were intended to simply be an indication of the proportions of each deck that involve healing, or deck manipulation, or whatever.

I honestly don't see another even vaguely sensible way of quantifying such complicated and varied powers (which as we all know will have different "values" depending on lots of other variables like number of heroes, what other cards are out, whether the Scholar's in play, or whatever).

Say Legacy has an arbitrary attack value of 2. How do you compare Ra's attack value to this? Sure, we'd all agree it should be higher than Legacy's 2, but how much higher? We'd never reach a consensus because we'd be using a fuzzy definition of "attack value". "Number of enemy-damaging cards in the deck" is a concrete value that no-one can argue with.
